articles.title: Maine students and residents planted 12,000 dune-grass stalks after two 2024 storms washed away dunes; in 2026, volunteers returned with 20,000 more to rebuild the beach
articles.summary: US News: A beach in Biddeford Pool, Maine, is being rebuilt with the help of dune grass. In March 2026, University of New England students and local volunteers.
articles.body: A beach in Biddeford Pool, Maine, is being rebuilt with the help of dune grass. In March 2026, University of New England students and local volunteers planted 20,000 stalks across about 20,000 square feet, continuing a restoration effort that began after severe storms damaged the dunes in 2024.The 2024 storms caused an estimated $90 million in damage across the Maine coast, according to the state, Univerisity of New England reported. The storms also washed away dunes at the Biddeford Pool beach, prompting the conservation trust and UNE to discuss ways to restore the damaged area.The 2026 effort was the second year in a row that UNE students worked with the trust. This time, the trust bought 66% more dune grass than the previous year. The 20,000 stalks are expected to cover about 20,000 square feet of beach.Students test how dune grass strengthen beachOn March 10, students from UNE Assistant Professor Will Kochtitzky’s Geographic Information System (GIS) course helped plant the grass. The volunteers made holes in the sand and buried the dune-grass stalks.The planting was also designed to support two new studies by UNE. The grass was planted in four separate sections, with stalks spaced either 18 inches apart or 12 inches apart. Kochtitzky’s classes will use drone analysis to study the different sections and determine which spacing works best.The project also added another part to UNE’s monitoring work around Biddeford Pool. Kochtitzky installed an anemometer on the conservation trust’s land. The device measures wind speed and direction near the dunes.“We will see wind speeds in real time, which is important because with the dunes you primarily have a lot of wind erosion,” Kochtitzky said.The wind data will be combined with information from other monitoring equipment in the area. A buoy off the Biddeford Pool coast measures wave height, while a monitoring station in a nearby pond measures water quality.“We're starting to fully understand almost every variable in the system. We're trying to put all of this together to better understand how these dunes are changing and evolving,” Kochtitzky said.How dune grass helps trap sandThe dune grass is being used as a natural way to help rebuild the dunes. Once planted, the stalks can grow while sand collects around them.The process was visible at the site this year. Biddeford Pool Conservation Trust President Lucie Fontein pointed towards the older dune grass planted during the previous year. The stalks appeared much shorter because sand had covered them during the winter.For Fontein, the sand covering the grass was a sign that the restoration was working as intended. “The sand is supposed to come in and get trapped and then the grass grows taller and, as a result, it traps more sand. Ultimately, the idea is for the dunes to get taller,” she said.The newly planted grass stretched for about 1,200 feet along the beach. The effort brought students and local residents together to work on the same section of coastline.The project also showed how quickly coastal areas can change after extreme weather. Sophie Cronin, an Environmental Studies student from the class of 2026, said she wanted to take part because the project allowed her to work directly with local residents. She also described the use of a natural solution to strengthen the coast as meaningful.“It’s meaningful,” Cronin said of the experience. “The community has been so supportive of us helping, because I think everyone recognizes that we really have an issue, and we want to try and find the best solutions.”Cronin said the 2024 storms had changed how some students viewed coastal damage. “I think that 2024 was kind of a wake-up call, especially for students who aren’t from Maine, that this is a very real thing and it can really be very jarring how quickly natural ecosystems can change,” she said.UNE and local residents continue restoration workFor other students, the project was also an opportunity to become more connected with the local community. John Montenegro, an Environmental Science student from the class of 2027, is from Houston. He said working alongside Biddeford residents helped him understand why the coastline mattered to them.“It’s pretty special to see this and be able to chat with them about why they’re passionate about this. To be out here also kind of shows them that it matters to us, too. I think that’s important to any community,” Montenegro said.UNE and the Biddeford Pool Conservation Trust have worked together for several years to study changes in the dunes. Their cooperation became particularly important after the January 2024 storms, when the dunes suffered significant damage.The planting project is now also providing material for further research. By comparing grass planted at different distances and combining drone observations with wind and wave measurements, UNE students will study how the dunes change over time.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: A Florida wife grew suspicious of her husband’s phone call; deputies found him in a Lowe’s parking lot about to buy $14,000 in gift cards
articles.summary: US News: Nassau County Sheriff’s Office deputies stopped a Florida resident at a retail parking lot on Thursday, preventing him from handing over $14,000 to ph.
articles.body: Nassau County Sheriff’s Office deputies stopped a Florida resident at a retail parking lot on Thursday, preventing him from handing over $14,000 to phone scammers. The intervention took place at a Lowe’s home improvement store on State Road 200 after the man’s wife overheard a suspicious phone call at their home. Worried by the pressure being put on her husband, she immediately contacted local law enforcement. Deputies arrived in the area and found the man sitting in his vehicle, preparing to follow the caller’s instructions to buy thousands of dollars in gift cards.Interception in retail parking lotAccording to a public report by local news outlet Action News Jax, the scammer had told the victim to purchase $14,000 worth of gift cards within two hours. The caller warned that failing to meet the deadline would result in the man’s personal accounts being hacked and compromised. Deputies reached the resident in the parking lot before he could enter the store or give the gift card codes to the scammer. Officers spoke with him, calmed the situation and explained how the caller was trying to trick him. The intervention protected the man’s money and stopped any payment from being made.Surge in regional fraud casesThe incident comes as financial scams continue to rise across northern Florida. Figures from the Nassau County Sheriff’s Office show that reported fraud cases have increased by about 80 per cent since 2021. Sheriff’s office records show deputies responded to 126 fraud cases in 2021. That figure rose to 227 cases in 2025. Data from the current year shows that officers in the county have already investigated at least 174 fraud complaints. The figures reflect a wider national trend recorded by the Federal Trade Commission, which says gift card payments remain one of the most common ways used by domestic and international scammers.Common tactics and warning signsIn a public safety warning after the incident, the Nassau County Sheriff’s Office listed several signs that can indicate a financial scam. Authorities stressed that legitimate businesses, police departments and government agencies will never demand immediate payment through store gift cards, wire transfers, peer-to-peer payment services such as Cash App, or cryptocurrency.Deputies warned residents to look out for several common pressure tactics:Urgency and strict deadlines: Scammers often create fake emergencies and give victims only minutes or hours to act, leaving little time to think or check the claims.Threats of legal or financial action: Callers may pretend to be officials and threaten immediate account suspension, large fines or arrest.Unusual payment methods: Requests for gift cards, prepaid debit cards or digital money transfers are major warning signs of fraud.Requests for sensitive information: Scammers may ask for PINs, passcodes or banking details while pretending they need the information for security checks.Police advise anyone who receives a suspicious payment request to end the call immediately. Residents should then contact their local police department or the relevant agency using an official phone number to check whether the claim is genuine.Protection measures and reportingThe Nassau County Sheriff’s Office is urging residents to take extra care when receiving unexpected phone calls, text messages or emails. Police advise people not to click links in unverified messages or provide personal information over the phone. Officials also point out that government agencies handle formal legal matters and bond payments through established procedures, not through unexpected phone calls or retail gift cards. People in Nassau County who have experienced attempted or completed fraud can contact the Sheriff’s Office non-emergency line at 904-225-5174. Fraud can also be reported to the Federal Trade Commission through its online portal at reportfraud.ftc.gov or to the FBI’s Internet Crime Complaint Center. Older adults who are dealing with financial exploitation can also seek help through the National Elder Fraud Hotline.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Trump says US will refill its petroleum reserves using Venezuelan oil
articles.summary: President Donald Trump says in a post that the ‘topping out’ process will ‌begin shortly.
articles.body:
United States President Donald Trump has said on social media that oil from a recently struck deal with Venezuela will be ⁠used to replenish the US Strategic Petroleum Reserve, an oil stockpile that the country keeps for emergencies and that has been drawn down sharply in ⁠recent years to respond to global supply disruptions and high fuel prices.

The US president wrote on Truth Social, the social media platform he owns, that the reserve had been made “virtually” empty, while blaming former US President Joe Biden.

Trump said in the post that the “topping out” process will ‌begin shortly, describing the Venezuelan oil as a “Gift from Venezuela to the People of the United States”.

It is unclear how quickly the Venezuela deal could provide oil for the reserve or deliver ⁠any near-term benefit to ⁠US motorists. The agreement Trump announced on Friday is aimed at reviving Venezuela’s battered oil industry, but it will require significant ⁠investment and infrastructure work before production can rise substantially.

The US reserve ⁠held about 290 million ⁠barrels as of August 21, near a 44-year low, after the US drew down its stockpile under both ‌the Biden and Trump administrations in response to global supply disruptions, including Russia’s invasion of Ukraine ‌and ‌the current US-Israel war on Iran.

The “historic” deal with Washington to hand over 65 billion barrels of Venezuelan oil will last 25 years and allow Venezuela to develop its oil industry while preserving “ownership of and sovereignty” of its resources, Venezuela’s interim President Delcy Rodriguez said in a televised address on Saturday.

The project envisages the development of 17 strategic oilfields with an initial production target of 1.5 million barrels per day, she said.

The broader plan also includes the development of eight greenfield oil blocks as part of a wider expansion of the country’s energy sector.

Under the deal, $19 from every barrel of oil produced and sold to the US will flow to Caracas, an arrangement that could be worth $209bn per year to Venezuela, depending on oil prices, Rodriguez said.

Venezuela will keep ownership of its natural resources “while leveraging capital, technology and operational expertise to support the recovery of a strategic industry that has been severely affected by sanctions”, she said.

Caracas has been under pressure to act in line with Washington’s demands since January, after US special forces abducted then-Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro and Venezuela’s Supreme Court handed leadership over to his vice president, Rodriguez.

articles.title: Rare manatees are turning up along the Texas coast this summer; some are lingering in busy marinas for freshwater, prompting warnings to boaters
articles.summary: US News: This summer, an unusual visitor has been making waves along the Texas coast: the Florida manatee. Multiple sightings have been reported from Galveston.
articles.body: This summer, an unusual visitor has been making waves along the Texas coast: the Florida manatee. Multiple sightings have been reported from Galveston to Port Mansfield, with some of the gentle giants lingering in busy harbours and marinas to drink from freshwater outflows. As temperatures soar, wildlife officials say the warm Gulf waters are drawing these rare marine mammals farther west than usual, but their presence in high-traffic boating areas is raising concerns. The Texas Marine Mammal Stranding Network (TMMSN) has issued warnings to boaters and is asking the public to report sightings while avoiding actions that could put the animals at greater risk, according to reports by the Houston Chronicle and Midland Reporter-Telegram, as well as information from TMMSN’s research program.Why manatees are in Texas nowFlorida, or West Indian, manatees are federally protected as a threatened species under the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service. They spend the winter in Florida’s warm springs and coastal waters, then migrate through the Gulf of Mexico during the summer, occasionally reaching Texas, Louisiana and even Mexico.“Texas is HOT and manatees are taking advantage of this warm water to expand their summer travels,” TMMSN wrote in a recent alert. The animals are drawn not only by temperature but also by freshwater sources. Manatees need to drink fresh water regularly, and along the Texas coast they often seek out freshwater outflows from marinas, boat ramps and industrial facilities.Sightings from Galveston to Port MansfieldTMMSN, a nonprofit that rescues, rehabilitates and monitors marine mammals along the Texas coast, said it is currently tracking a number of recent manatee sightings from Galveston to Port Mansfield. Many have been observed drinking from freshwater outflows and spending time in busy harbours or marinas, where boat traffic can put them at risk.On July 28, the Port Aransas South Jetty shared a video of a manatee spotted at various times in the Port Aransas harbour. The clip shows the animal drinking freshwater beside a boat, earning it the nickname “plus-sized mermaid” from one commenter. While the sighting delighted locals, it also underscored how closely manatees are now sharing space with recreational and commercial vessels.Why marinas are both a lure and a dangerFor manatees, marinas and boat ramps can be ideal rest stops: they offer calm water, shade from docks and, crucially, access to freshwater. But these same areas are often crowded with boats, jet skis and other watercraft moving at speed.Boat strikes remain one of the biggest threats to Florida manatees, along with habitat loss and starvation caused by pollution. Manatees are large, heavy and slow-moving, yet they can be surprisingly difficult to spot in the water, especially in choppy or murky conditions. When they linger in busy harbors, the risk of collision rises sharply.That reality was highlighted about a year ago, when a manatee near the Port Aransas ferry landings temporarily halted a $64 million project to upgrade ferry ramps and landings on the Mustang Island side of the channel. The incident showed how even routine coastal infrastructure work can be complicated by the presence of these protected animals.What officials are asking boaters and the public to doTMMSN and the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service are urging boaters to watch for manatees, especially in areas where freshwater outflows are known to attract them. Simple steps can make a big difference: Slow down in marinas, channels and near freshwater discharges; keep a sharp lookout for large, dark shapes just below the surface; and give manatees plenty of space and avoid chasing or crowding them.The network is also asking the public to report every manatee sighting. People can call TMMSN at 1-800-9MAMMAL (1-800-962-6625) or visit DolphinRescue.org to log live sightings, injured manatees or dead animals. Photos taken from a safe distance can help researchers identify individual animals, particularly those with distinctive scars.Don’t offer freshwater, let them find it naturallyOne of the most important, and counterintuitive, requests from TMMSN is this: do not intentionally provide freshwater to manatees with hoses or other sources.“You can help keep them safe during their Texas stay by never intentionally providing fresh water for manatees via hoses or other sources,” the organisation advises. “It can make them more susceptible to injury from boats and encourage the manatees to stay in the areas they have migrated to, which can become a serious problem for their health.”When manatees become accustomed to easy freshwater at busy marinas, they may linger longer in high-risk zones instead of moving on to safer, more natural areas. Over time, that behaviour can increase their exposure to boat strikes, entanglement and other human-related threats.Tracking manatees to protect themTo better understand manatee presence, migration and well-being in Texas, TMMSN maintains a sighting database that documents locations and movement patterns of West Indian manatees in state waters. This long-term dataset helps researchers assess health trends, identify critical habitats and inform conservation management.TMMSN’s research program, which has operated along the Texas coast since 1980, also collects data and biological samples from stranded marine mammals, conducts photographic identification surveys and publishes findings to advance marine mammal science. Manatee documentation is one piece of a broader effort that includes bottlenose dolphin abundance estimates, habitat-use studies and assessments of human-induced injury or mortality.A rare but recurring summer phenomenonManatee sightings in Texas are uncommon but not unprecedented. Every summer, a small number of individuals wander into state waters as they follow warm currents and search for food and freshwater. Most move on after a few days or weeks, but some linger longer, especially if they find reliable freshwater sources and sheltered areas.For coastal residents and visitors, a manatee sighting is a special event, a chance to see one of the ocean’s most iconic and gentle mammals up close. But it also comes with responsibility. By slowing down, staying alert and reporting sightings, Texans can help ensure that these rare summer visitors leave the coast as safely as they arrived.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Niger attempted coup: Russia says it helped to repel attack
articles.summary: Soldiers tried to attack a key military base early on Saturday morning, authorities say, but were thwarted.
articles.body:
Russia has said its forces helped to repel Saturday's attempted coup in Niger.

Explosions and gunfire rang out across capital, Niamey, early in the morning, including at a key military airbase and the presidential palace.

Hours later, Niger's authorities said the rebellion had been contained.

Nigerien forces had repelled the attack "with the assistance of servicemen of the African Corps of the Russian Ministry of Defence", the foreign ministry in Moscow said on Sunday.

The ministry also said it would continue to support Niger in its fight against "extremists", but that the situation was now under the control of the legitimate authorities headed by President [Gen Abdourahmane] Tiani".

Russia's African Corps has become a key security partner for multiple military governments in the Sahel, who have been struggling to contain long-running jihadist insurgencies.

War ‘tour’, football and graffiti: How Russia is trying to influence Africa

The Alliance of Sahel States - composed of Niger, Mali and Burkina Faso - said the attempted coup was "a betrayal by a group of soldiers involved in an attempt at destabilisation".

The authorities have not said how many soldiers were involved in the attempted coup, nor how many casualties there were.

Niger's military ruler, Gen Tiani, who was sworn in as its president last year after he deposed its elected leader, has also not publicly addressed the incident.

The nation's state broadcaster showed footage of several alleged mutineers being arrested by the Presidential Guard.

On Sunday, Niger Press Agency reported that commercial activity was returning to normal, with petrol stations, shops and other businesses reopening.

Supporters of the government gathered at a public square in central Niamey in support of the security forces and Tiani's government.

Air Base 101, the military site attacked on Saturday, is part of the Diori Hamani airport complex.

It hosts Nigerien military aircraft and drones, as well as an Alliance of Sahel States counter-terrorism unit. Russian and Italian forces are also based there, according to news agency Reuters.

Niger, Mali and Burkina Faso are all military-ruled countries that have cut ties with Western partners and strengthened their co-operation with Russia.

But jihadist violence remains widespread in all three countries, despite the shift in alliances.

For Niger's government, Saturday's mutiny highlights that the military is dealing not only with an external insurgency, but also signs of discontent within its own ranks.

The airbase where the mutiny began had itself been targeted twice by jihadists this year – once by an Islamic State affiliate and later by an al-Qaeda affiliate.

Nigerien authorities say security forces have increased patrols around key sites in Niamey following the attempted takeover, including the main airport entrance and the presidential pavilion.

articles.title: Woman injured in fatal police pursuit crash near Stratford-upon-Avon dies
articles.summary: She had been driving a car which was involved in a collision with an Audi being chased by police.
articles.body:
A woman who was critically injured when her car was in collision with a vehicle involved in a police pursuit has died.

The 62-year-old was the driver of a Ford Puma which collided with an Audi A3 on the A439 Warwick Road near Stratford-upon-Avon in Warwickshire on Monday.

The driver of the Audi, a 19-year-old man, died at the scene. The Audi was being followed by police officers after it had earlier failed to pull over when requested to do so.

The Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC) has begun an investigation and said thoughts were with the friends and families of both those who died. The families have requested privacy, a statement said.

"We can confirm that a woman who was critically injured in a road traffic incident in Warwick Road, Stratford-upon-Avon on Monday (24 Aug) has, sadly, died," the statement said.

"The 62-year-old woman's Ford Puma was in collision with a black Audi A3 car which had been pursued by officers from Warwickshire Police.

"Our thoughts are with the friends and families of both those who have died and both families have requested privacy at this difficult time."

Warwickshire Police was also contacted for a comment, but said it was directing inquiries to the IOPC. It has referred the crash to the police complaints watchdog because a death had occurred following police contact.

Police previously said the pursuit began shortly before 17:30 BST on Birmingham Road when officers attempted to stop the Audi, but the driver failed to pull over.

The crash happened about 15 minutes later, the force said.

The Ford driver, initially reported to be in her 70s, was taken to hospital along with another woman, who had been a passenger in the Ford.

West Midlands Ambulance Service said the second woman had suffered serious injuries, but they were not thought to be life threatening.

Injuries to another patient from the Ford were not believed to be serious.

After failing to stop, the Audi made off in the direction of the A46 before travelling back towards Stratford on the A439.

A number of other cars were damaged during the pursuit, police said.

Warwick Road was closed on Monday from the Marraway roundabout to its junction with Ingon Lane and Sand Barn Lane, with the stretch remaining shut on Tuesday morning.

Manuela Perteghella, Liberal Democrat MP for Stratford-on-Avon, said on Tuesday the incdent was "incredibly tragic".

"My thoughts are with the families of all those impacted. We must now let the investigation take its course."

The IOPC is asking anyone who may have footage of the Audi or the pursuit to contact them.

articles.title: Meet Marcus Klepacki, the 19-year-old Phoenix musician who learned to play an acoustic drum kit with one arm and is now debuting his own band
articles.summary: US News: Nineteen-year-old Phoenix musician Marcus Klepacki is preparing for his first official public performance with his new rock band, Third Man Factor, at.
articles.body: Nineteen-year-old Phoenix musician Marcus Klepacki is preparing for his first official public performance with his new rock band, Third Man Factor, at Tempe’s historic Yucca Tap Room. What makes the performance unusual is not only the venue but also the way Klepacki plays. Born without a right arm and without a thumb on his left hand, the 19-year-old plays a standard acoustic drum kit without any major changes, using only one arm. According to reports from the Phoenix New Times and coverage published by Hoodline, Klepacki finds comparisons with Def Leppard drummer Rick Allen amusing, but says their approaches are very different. Allen lost his left arm in a 1984 car crash and later used a specially designed electronic drum system with foot pedals. Klepacki, however, plays entirely on acoustic drums, relying on physical skill and his own playing technique. "I think people need to know that Marcus, he's not good for having one arm; he's just good," Chuck Savale, a music instructor who coached Klepacki, told the Phoenix New Times.Early health battles and musical trainingKlepacki’s journey to the stage has followed years of serious health problems. He was diagnosed with scoliosis at age 3 and wore a corrective back brace from kindergarten until he entered high school. At age 7, he was diagnosed with leukaemia and underwent three and a half years of chemotherapy. In 2021, Dr Greg White, head of paediatric spinal surgery at Phoenix Children’s Hospital, performed surgery to correct Klepacki’s spine. White also plays bass in local cover band Central Line. In 2024, he invited Klepacki’s former music group to open for his band at Copper Blues Live in Desert Ridge. Throughout his medical challenges, his parents, Alex and Melissa Klepacki, made sure he could take part in normal childhood activities. His formal music education began at around age 10 when he started lessons at Alice Cooper’s Solid Rock Teen Centers, a Phoenix non-profit that provides free arts training to young people. Reports by the Phoenix New Times explain how Savale taught Klepacki by practising with only one arm himself. This helped him understand techniques that could produce a full and strong sound. Within a few years, Klepacki had learned difficult drumming patterns, including the famous "Purdie shuffle" created by legendary session drummer Bernard Purdie. The rhythm uses a half-time beat with triplet hi-hat patterns and soft snare notes. "It blew my mind when I saw Marcus do that," Savale told reporters, adding that the young drummer quickly moved beyond his own technical abilities.Formation of Third Man FactorKlepacki gained more performance experience by joining marching and concert bands at Shadow Mountain High School in Phoenix. He also played drums at around half a dozen showcases for Alice Cooper charity events. Third Man Factor’s lineup came together mainly through Arizona State University’s Bachelor of Arts in Popular Music programme at the Herberger Institute for Design and the Arts. Alongside Klepacki on drums are lead vocalist Fletcher Placko, guitarists Chris Sanchez and Ben Pakula, and bassist Noah Paz. Speaking to the Phoenix New Times, Placko praised Klepacki’s team spirit and natural ability. He said the other musicians quickly respected his talent when they played together during university classes. The band takes inspiration from 1990s alternative rock and grunge. Klepacki’s own drumming influences include Rush’s Neil Peart, Led Zeppelin’s John Bonham, The Police’s Stewart Copeland, Buddy Rich and The White Stripes’ Meg White.Stage debut at Yucca Tap RoomThe chance to perform at Yucca Tap Room came after the mother of the frontman of local band The Black Hole saw Klepacki play at an open-mic event at the Solid Rock Teen Center. She later offered him a place on the bill, according to Hoodline and Phoenix New Times reports. Open since the 1960s, Yucca Tap Room is Tempe’s oldest active live music venue. Over the years, it has helped launch and support independent rock and punk bands from across the East Valley. The Sunday afternoon show features Third Man Factor alongside a six-band lineup. The bill includes headliners The Black Hole, Band of Fools, the Hard Bop Group, Just About Halfway and Rino. Looking ahead, Klepacki hopes to build a long-term career in music. He is considering work as a touring performer, session musician or record producer. Reflecting on his experiences and future, Klepacki told the Phoenix New Times: "Part of my attitude is: I went through some of the hardest things people could go through early on."Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Zambian opposition leader charged with treason
articles.summary: Mundubile had previously gone into hiding at a United Nations building in Zambia's capital.
articles.body:
Zambian opposition leader Brian Mundubile has been charged with treason, his lawyer has said amid heightened political tensions in the country.

Mundubile was arrested on Thursday, after a deadly raid by the authorities led the opposition politician to go into hiding.

He had disputed the results of the country's recent presidential election, which saw incumbent President Hakainde Hichilema securing a second term.

The authorities then accused Mundubile's NRPUP party of planning an armed insurgency, which it denied.

On Saturday night, Mundubile's lawyer Milner Katolo announced that his client had been charged with treason. The opposition leader looks forward to answering the accusation in court, Katolo told the Zambian Eye .

The lawyer said 17 others, including Mundubile's running mate Makebi Zulu, had also been charged with treason.

Mundubile gained 38% of the vote in the 13 August election, while Hichilema secured 60%, official results show.

The government said they seized weapons during the raid.

Following the raid, Mundubile and Zulu took refuge at a United Nations building in the city. The pair were detained after the president put pressure on the UN to hand them over.

The opposition was unable to mount a legal challenge to the election outcome as the courts were sealed off by the authorities on Monday, the final day that a case could be filed.

Hichilema is due to be sworn in for a second term on 1 September.

Regional and international observers described the election day as largely peaceful, but Zambia's Human Rights Commission has called for accountability over people whose whereabouts remain unknown following arrests and security operations around the elections.

articles.title: 'Oldest trick in RSS playbook': Owaisi attacks Mohan Bhagwat over Hindu-Muslim remarks
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: AIMIM president Asaduddin Owaisi on Sunday criticised RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat over his remarks on Hindu-Muslim unity, alleging that the RSS.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: AIMIM president Asaduddin Owaisi on Sunday criticised RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat over his remarks on Hindu-Muslim unity, alleging that the RSS projects a different image of itself to the world while the writings of its key thinkers reflect a different view of minorities.Owaisi's remarks came a day after Bhagwat, speaking at at event in New York, said that a Hindu who believes Muslims should not live in India would not remain a Hindu.Reacting to the remarks, Owaisi said, “This is the oldest trick in the RSS playbook: some words are for the world, and some are for its own members. The RSS has never disavowed its key thinkers and writers. What do they say about Muslims and other minorities?”Owaisi referred to a biography of RSS founder K B Hedgewar, published by the RSS, to claim that Hedgewar had opposed the Congress's emphasis on Hindu-Muslim unity.Quoting from the biography, Owaisi said, “Gandhiji worked constantly with one eye on Hindu-Muslim unity... But Doctorji sensed danger in that move. In fact, he did not even relish the newfangled slogan of 'Hindu-Muslim Unity'.”The AIMIM chief also cited former RSS chief M S Golwalkar's writings, referring to his book Bunch of Thoughts and its chapter titled 'Internal Threats'.“Golwalkar's 'Bunch of Thoughts' has a long chapter titled 'Internal Threats', in which Muslim and Christian citizens of India are described as threats number one and two, respectively,” Owaisi said.He also referred to Golwalkar's statement that the Sangh was “inspired by one flag (saffron), one leader and one ideology”.Owaisi alleged that the RSS did not contribute to India's freedom struggle and claimed that Hedgewar left the Congress because he opposed the participation of different religious communities in the anti-British movement led by Mahatma Gandhi.Owaisi also invoked the 2002 Gujarat riots while criticising the RSS, asking, “Should we forget what happened to the Muslims of Gujarat under the RSS's proxy rule?”He alleged that Muslims and Christians continued to face discrimination and claimed that Muslims were being subjected to Hindu law in the name of the Uniform Civil Code, while Christians were being targeted through “draconian” anti-conversion laws.The AIMIM chief also raised concerns over the alleged misuse of laws such as the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA).Earlier on Saturday, addressing the ‘One World One Humanity’ event in New York, Bhagwat said different religions may follow different paths, but humanity and truth remain one. “We come from a society that believes humanity is one,” he said.“If any Hindu thinks that there should be no Muslim in Bharat, he will not remain Hindu. If you want to call yourself Hindu, you must believe that all paths are leading to the same goal and that every human has dignity. There is no difference between human beings,” Bhagwat had added.Bhagwat also used the occasion to speak about perceptions of the RSS. He said the organisation was often viewed through narratives that, in his view, did not reflect its work on the ground."There are many perceptions created by wrong narratives. But when you come and see us from inside, all those will be disbelieved in the day."The RSS chief was speaking in New York as he began a three-nation global outreach tour covering the United States, Canada and the United Kingdom. The visit has been organised as part of the organisation's centenary year celebrations, following invitations from overseas local organisations.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Trump threatens to report journalist Kristen Welker to broadcast regulator
articles.summary: The Federal Communications Commission under Trump has tried to target news outlets for spreading ‘fake’ news.
articles.body:
United States President Donald Trump says he will report a prominent NBC television journalist to the federal agency in charge of regulating broadcast news outlets for “rebuke or punishment”.

In a post on Truth Social on Sunday, Trump took issue with Kristen Welker’s characterisation of his endorsements of electoral candidates as having “mixed results” in the primaries leading up to November’s elections.

“How can anyone be allowed to say this, working for freely given public airwaves?” Trump wrote. He also posted, without any attribution of where he got the data, a chart showing 98 percent of the candidates he endorsed had won their elections.

“Because of this purposeful inaccuracy, she will be reported to the FCC,” the Federal Communications Commission, he said.

Welker hosted the 2020 presidential election debate between Trump and former President Joe Biden and currently hosts NBC’s weekly news programme Meet the Press.

In June, Welker had a one-on-one interview with Trump that ended in a heated exchange as she pressed the Republican president on continuing to claim the Democratic Party had cheated in the 2020 presidential election, in which Biden defeated Trump.

“Your elections are crooked, and you’re crooked, and Meet the Press is crooked and so is ABC and CBS and CNN. You’re one-sided crooked networks,” Trump said shortly before pulling off his microphone and leaving the interview.

Trump, who has long had a tumultuous relationship with those US television news networks, has increasingly threatened to use the FCC to target what he says is false news.

This month, ABC News’s owner, Disney, sued the FCC , saying the agency was conducting an early licence review of eight of the network’s stations, a move that it said was “retaliation” against it. ABC said the FCC was seeking “a media industry too fearful of official reprisal to report the news freely”.

The review followed a row between the network and the FCC after Trump and his wife Melania called on it to fire late-night TV host Jimmy Kimmel over a joke he had made about her.

President Trump has also filed several multibillion-dollar civil lawsuits against news outlets alleging defamation. Last year, he filed a $10bn lawsuit against the BBC, which he said unfairly edited a clip of him speaking just before his supporters stormed the US Capitol on January 6, 2021, to make it seem like he had called for violence.

Trump sued The New York Times for $15bn and The Wall Street Journal for $10bn, alleging defamation over reporting on issues such as how he amassed his wealth and his relationship to convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein. A judge threw out the case against The Wall Street Journal. Trump refiled the case against The New York Times after a judge dismissed the first complaint against the newspaper last year.

Attempts to compel reporters to reveal sources

The warning from Trump also comes as his administration has taken the rare step of using the courts to try to pressure journalists into giving up confidential sources for stories that have pointed out wrongdoing.

This month, The New York Times said agents from the FBI showed up at the home of one of its reporters in February to deliver a subpoena seeking cooperation for an investigation into a story that revealed how a secret US Navy SEALs mission in North Korea had ended up with them opening fire on a North Korean boat.

In July, the US Department of Justice also tried to subpoena three other journalists from the newspaper after they reported on security concerns with the president’s new Air Force One jet. Investigators were seeking phone records of the journalists but withdrew the requests after a federal judge upbraided the tactic in court, saying they were violating the First Amendment, a provision in the US Constitution that protects freedom of the press.

Reporters at The Wall Street Journal and The Washington Post have also been subpoenaed in recent months for national security coverage, including for reporting on internal Pentagon warnings about the US-Israel war on Iran.

News media freedom groups like the Committee to Protect Journalists have criticised the Trump administration for targeting critical media. In April, the group Reporters Sans Frontieres, or Reporters Without Borders, said the US has fallen to a “historic low” in its annual global press freedom rankings, dropping from 57th in the world to 64th.

articles.title: Bangladesh says no risk in joining Mecca defence pact with Saudi Arabia, Pakistan, Turkiye
articles.summary: South Asia News: Bangladesh on Sunday said it sees no risk in joining the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement with Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkiye, arguing that particip.
articles.body: Bangladesh on Sunday said it sees no risk in joining the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement with Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkiye, arguing that participation in the pact would not limit its engagement with other international partners, news agency PTI reported.State minister for foreign affairs Humaiun Kobir said Dhaka was holding discussions on the issue and that the talks were “progressing positively” with its bilateral partners. He said Bangladesh would pursue a flexible foreign policy while balancing its international relationships.“This is a unique pact that presents new opportunities,” Kobir told reporters after a meeting with Saudi Ambassador to Bangladesh Abdullah Zafer bin Abiyah.Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkiye signed the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement on August 7 amid heightened security concerns in West Asia. The pact establishes a framework for collective deterrence and states that an armed attack against any one of the three signatories would be regarded as an attack against all.India has said it is closely monitoring developments related to the pact and will take necessary steps to safeguard its security interests.Dhaka says pact will not restrict other alliancesKobir said joining one area of security cooperation would not prevent Bangladesh from contributing to other alliances or partnerships. He added that during his recent visit to Jeddah, he discussed the pact with several officials, including Saudi Foreign Minister Prince Faisal bin Farhan Al Saud, and received a “very positive” response.Foreign minister Khalilur Rahman had earlier told Parliament that Bangladesh viewed the pact positively and would consider joining if it received an invitation. However, he said Dhaka had not yet received any formal offer to join the agreement.Experts warn of possible foreign policy complicationsBangladeshi foreign policy experts and former diplomats have expressed reservations about Dhaka joining the military pact, saying it could mark a departure from the country's longstanding policy of non-alignment and potentially complicate ties with India.Former ambassador Mahfuzur Rahman said the pact may be important for Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkiye but was not essential for Bangladesh, which faces little likelihood of being drawn into the kinds of conflicts involving the existing members.Another former diplomat, Humayun Kabir, said Bangladesh would need to assess whether the security interests of the pact's members align with its own national, economic and strategic interests.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Nottingham attack mum tells of trauma of fighting early release plan
articles.summary: Emma Webber says victim's families had faced "trauma" to get killers barred from the scheme.
articles.body:
The mother of a man stabbed to death in the Nottingham attacks has cautiously welcomed a change to the early prisoner release scheme which should mean her son's killer will not now qualify.

The plan to ease prison congestion had initially included those convicted of manslaughter but, following a high profile outcry, Prime Minister Andy Burnham said this category of offender had been ruled out .

Barnaby Webber was one of three people killed by paranoid schizophrenic Valdo Calocane in 2023. He was subsequently convicted of manslaughter on the grounds of diminished responsibility.

Emma Webber said while the change was "the right thing", the families had faced "trauma" to get this point.

The government has been looking for ways to ease pressure in a prison system that is more than 97% full in England and Wales.

Opposition to the early release scheme centred on the family and former colleagues of PC Andrew Harper - who was dragged to his death in 2019 - and the potential release of two of the three people responsible.

But on Saturday more than 30 affected families, including the Webbers, signed a letter to Justice Secretary Alex Norris, which said they felt victims were "being asked to bear the consequences of the prison capacity crisis".

Calocane's manslaughter conviction was controversial for the families who had wanted him tried for murder.

He was sentenced to be detained at a high-security hospital. At the time the judge said it would probably be for the rest of his life.

Reacting to the announcement, Emma Webber said: "I'm glad it has happened, it is the right thing.

"But I'll tell you what wasn't the right thing, the trauma of victims, who have been through so much already, have had to go through to fight for this.

"Petitions, doing news interviews, having to talk about the terrible losses we have suffered and there are dozens of us that have had to do this.

"I try not to be always confrontational and always fighting but as much as I try not to, it seems to be the only way that things are getting done.

"Everything we have done as families in the Nottingham attacks has come at such great cost and yes we are getting results but we shouldn't have had to do any of it at all."

She said the controversy reflected wider problems with funding across the justice system.

"The fact that we were even having to consider releasing people who had taken lives and destroyed families and communities early from their sentences is abhorrent.

"I stand by what I said yesterday - it is morally bankrupt."

She also confirmed after making a call to meet ministers some weeks ago, they had now received an invitation to meet with Justice Secretary Alex Norris, where their concerns would be raised.

articles.title: He died at 23 after fighting in the Korean War; nearly 74 years later Willie Estrada’s family is still pushing for him to receive the Medal of Honor
articles.summary: US News: Nearly 74 years after Sergeant Willie Noriega Estrada died while protecting his tank crew during the Korean War, his family is still working to have h.
articles.body: Nearly 74 years after Sergeant Willie Noriega Estrada died while protecting his tank crew during the Korean War, his family is still working to have his military award upgraded to the Medal of Honor. The New Mexico native was 23 when he was killed in action on 22 September 1952 near Bongowol, North Korea. He became the first draftee from Otero County to receive the Distinguished Service Cross, the US Army’s second-highest award for extraordinary heroism. According to reporting by the Carlsbad Current-Argus, his brothers Mario Estrada and Pete Estrada remain determined to make sure his actions receive the country’s highest military honour.Last stand at Hill 223In September 1952, Sergeant Estrada was a tank commander with Company C of the 245th Medium Tank Battalion, attached to the 45th Infantry Division. During a fierce overnight battle involving an estimated 2,000 enemy troops, his unit came under heavy artillery and anti-tank fire. Military records and historical accounts preserved by Honor States describe how Estrada’s tank crew fought enemy forces for 15 hours to protect nearby infantry positions. As enemy bazooka rounds began hitting and penetrating the tanks, Estrada ordered a second tank nearby to pull back to safety while he stayed behind to cover its retreat. Estrada suffered terrible injuries, including losing an arm after a shaped-charge round pierced his tank turret. Despite his wounds, he continued firing his machine gun to slow the advancing enemy forces. When friendly troops reached the hill the next morning, they found Estrada alive inside the damaged tank. He died from severe blood loss shortly after rescue teams arrived. Soldiers approaching the position also found Chinese graffiti written on the tank’s steel hull that read "Brave Fighter". It had been left by enemy troops who had passed the position.Legacy and decorations in New MexicoEstrada remains the most decorated military service member in Otero County’s history. In addition to the Distinguished Service Cross, his awards include the Silver Star with Oak Leaf Cluster, the Purple Heart, the Air Medal with Oak Leaf Cluster and the Republic of Korea Presidential Unit Citation. His hometown of Alamogordo honoured him on 3 June 2004 by naming its municipal facility the Willie Estrada Memorial Civic Center. His name has also been given to military sites outside New Mexico, including a street at Fort Knox, Kentucky, and an Army training camp in South Korea. Despite these honours, his family believes his actions deserve the Medal of Honor. Because many decades have passed since the war, securing an upgrade requires congressional action or presidential approval.The legal path to an award upgradeUpgrading a military award for bravery many decades after a war involves a detailed review by the US Department of Defense and Congress. Under federal military rules, requests to upgrade awards must provide new and previously unavailable historical evidence or show that an administrative error stopped the original recommendation from being properly considered.The process usually involves:Congressional sponsorship: A member of Congress must introduce special waiver legislation to get around the normal time limits set under Title 10 of the United States Code.Service branch review: The Senior Army Board for Correction of Military Records examines battle reports, statements from surviving crew members and recommendations from commanders.Department approval: The Secretary of the Army and Secretary of Defense must formally support the upgraded award.Presidential authorisation: The Medal of Honor is ultimately presented by the President of the United States on behalf of Congress.Mario and Pete Estrada continue to collect military records and work with veterans’ advocacy groups as they seek support from lawmakers for a formal congressional review. The family says its campaign is not about adding another decoration, but about completing the official record of a soldier who gave his life to protect his fellow crew members on a remote Korean ridge.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.summary: News News: NEW DELHI: In an uphill task in the mountain ranges of Himalayas, Indian Army Aviation pilots carried out a “daring high-casualty evacuation” with the.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: In an uphill task in the mountain ranges of Himalayas, Indian Army Aviation pilots carried out a “daring high-casualty evacuation” with their helicopter at 18,600 feet near the Nun Kun massif, a mountain group in the Zanskar range in Kargil district of Ladakh, on Saturday.“Indian Army Aviation pilots evacuated a casualty from an extremely challenging slope with no landing space and strong winds,” Fire & Fury Corps of the Army posted on X.The rescue area consisted of an exceptionally steep, snow-covered slope battered by severe winds, leaving absolutely no flat ground for a traditional landing.“The aviators operated at an altitude where the reduced atmospheric density severely impairs engine performance and robs rotor blades of their lift. To carry out the mission, the rescue crew had to take drastic measures to prepare for the ascent. The rescue team stripped the aircraft of all non-essential equipment to lighten the load to the absolute minimum weight required for flight, it said.With zero room for error, the pilots maintained a perilous hover, balancing the helicopter by touching down with only one skid on the slope while keeping the rest of the aircraft airborne.Headquartered in Leh, Fire & Fury Corps was created specifically to guard India’s highly sensitive northern and western borders. The corps is responsible for defending the toughest and most hostile military frontiers in the world, including the Siachen Glacier, Zojila, Kargil, Daulat Beg Oldie (DBO), and Demchok. It is the only military formation in the world that regularly deploys and maintains mechanised forces (such as tanks and infantry combat vehicles) at such extreme high-altitude and sub-zero environments.Saturday’s challenging mission, undertaken at the last available landing window of the day, stands as a testament to the skill, courage and compassion of Indian Army Aviation.

articles.title: What Meta's new teen restrictions mean for young people
articles.summary: Meta's new teen accounts settlement sets a default two-hour daily limit on Instagram and Facebook, plus night mode and school mode restrictions.
articles.body: If you have ever asked a teenager to put down a phone and heard, "Just one more minute," you already know how hard screen limits can be to enforce. Now Meta has agreed to a sweeping child-safety settlement that could reshape how teens use Facebook and Instagram across much of the United States. A judge approved the agreement on Aug. 27. Under the deal, Meta will put a default two-hour daily cap on teen use of Facebook and Instagram combined. It will also restrict most app access overnight. Meanwhile, parents will get stronger control over settings teens may want to change. The agreement goes well beyond a screen time reminder. Here's what will change, how the limits work, what Meta told CyberGuy and what parents can do now. Missed CyberGuy LIVE? Watch the Protect Your Money replay Our free CyberGuy LIVE class, Protect Your Money From Today’s Biggest Threats , has ended, but you can still watch the full replay and download our financial protection checklist. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson walks you through five simple ways to help defend yourself against AI scams, fraud, identity theft and financial hacks. You’ll learn how to set up bank alerts, strengthen your account logins, protect your phone number, freeze your credit and help secure your retirement savings against unauthorized transfers. No technical experience is needed. Get the free replay and checklist now at CyberGuyLive.com TOO MUCH SCREEN TIME MAY TRIGGER LASTING BRAIN DELAYS, TOP HEALTH OFFICIAL WARNS How Meta's new restrictions could change a teen's day With the judge's approval, the agreement is now in effect, but the new protections will roll out over the coming months. Most of the major requirements have a six-month compliance deadline, while some features are due sooner. Here's how the biggest changes break down for teens and parents. A two-hour limit across Facebook and Instagram Meta will apply a default two-hour daily limit across Facebook and Instagram combined. Time spent scrolling on either app counts toward the total. In addition, Meta says it will count usage across multiple accounts when it detects that one teen operates more than one account. Direct messaging, time spent in settings and qualifying long-form audio or video are excluded from the two-hour limit. Under the agreement, qualifying long-form content generally means audio or video that lasts at least 22 minutes and has not been artificially extended. A teen can only turn off the two-hour limit with a parent's permission. That creates a much firmer stopping point than another reminder that can be dismissed. Night Mode blocks most overnight use Night Mode will block most Facebook and Instagram activity from midnight to 6 a.m. During that window, teens will no longer be able to view or post to areas such as Feed, Stories, Explore or Reels. Direct messaging will remain available. That exception lets teens continue communicating with friends and family. For families dealing with late-night scrolling, this could create a clearer boundary without requiring someone to change the setting every evening. Meta will also disable push notifications by default from 10 p.m. to 7 a.m., except for urgent account security or platform integrity alerts. Parents using supervision can change that setting. School Mode cuts back notifications School Mode focuses on daytime distractions. From 8 a.m. to 3 p.m. Monday through Friday between Aug. 15 and June 15, Meta will mute most push notifications by default. However, teens will still be able to receive direct messages. Meta will also allow account security and safety alerts during those hours. The idea is simple. A school day should come with fewer reasons to keep checking Instagram or Facebook. Screen-time prompts arrive every 15 minutes Meta will also add more frequent reminders. Teens will receive a prompt after every 15 minutes of continuous screen time on Facebook or Instagram. In addition, Meta will send prompts when total daily use reaches 60 minutes and again at 90 minutes. The settlement requires these prompts and pauses to be implemented within four months of the agreement's effective date. Those alerts arrive before a teen reaches the two-hour limit. As a result, the hard cap becomes the final boundary rather than the first warning. Teens get more control over what they see The agreement also changes parts of the viewing experience. Teens will be able to choose a non-personalized feed as their default. That feed will avoid Meta's recommendation systems when deciding what to show next. Parents using supervision will be able to require that setting. Meta will also periodically remind teens that the option exists. Meanwhile, teens will be able to turn off autoplay. Parents will be able to require that setting too. With autoplay disabled, another piece of content will no longer begin automatically. The teen will need to tap or swipe to continue. NEW MEXICO SEEKS MASSIVE PENALTY FROM META AFTER JURY FOUND TECH GIANT LIABLE FOR ENDANGERING CHILDREN Likes and appearance filters also change Meta will hide like and reaction totals by default for teen accounts. That applies to a teen's own posts as well as content posted by other people. The company is also expanding its restrictions on appearance filters. Meta already blocks teens from using cosmetic surgery filters. Under the agreement, teens will also lose access to what Meta calls extreme makeup filters. These changes target parts of the social media experience that can keep attention focused on appearance and social feedback. Meta plans stronger age checks Age verification sits at the center of these protections. A teen limit only works if the platform correctly identifies the person behind the account. Meta says it will invest in stronger technology to find accounts that may belong to children under 13. The company also plans to improve systems that identify users ages 13 to 17 who enter an adult birthday. Once Meta identifies those accounts, it can place them into experiences designed for teens. Still, age detection remains one of the biggest tests ahead. A system that regularly mistakes teens for adults could weaken many of the protections in the agreement. Parents get more alerts and controls Meta also plans to expand its parental supervision tools. For example, parents will receive a notification when a teen links a secondary account. The company also plans alerts involving interactions with accounts it considers potentially suspicious. In addition, parents will get periodic updates about their teen's usage and attempts to change protective settings. Those alerts could make it easier to catch changes without constantly checking a teen's account. Meta's Teen Accounts already laid the groundwork Meta began rolling out Teen Accounts in 2024. Those accounts brought automatic protections to younger Instagram users and added more control for parents. Meta later expanded its teen safety approach across more of its services. CyberGuy previously covered Meta's expansion of Teen Accounts to Facebook and Messenger. Earlier tools leaned more heavily on reminders and configurable controls. By comparison, the settlement creates stronger defaults. A teen who reaches the two-hour combined limit will need a parent's permission to turn it off. For a household where "five more minutes" somehow turns into another hour, that could feel very different. Why TikTok and YouTube are tied to Meta's payout Meta describes the financial package as approximately $18 billion. Participating states would receive about 70% of the allocated payment, or roughly $12.7 billion, over 10 years. The remaining 30%, about $5.3 billion, depends on TikTok and YouTube meeting two conditions. First, both companies would need to implement a one-hour Daily Limit, Night Mode and age-assurance measures. Second, each would need to make a matching financial payment. Half of Meta's remaining funds would be tied to YouTube's payment. The other half would depend on TikTok. Meta argues that restricting teens on one platform has limited impact if they can immediately move to another app. That helps explain why two of its biggest rivals play such a prominent role in the agreement. The executed agreement also includes Snap in the broader industry-adoption framework. However, Meta's public explanation ties the matching financial-payment requirement specifically to TikTok and YouTube. Meta calls for an industry-wide approach Meta responded to CyberGuy with additional information about the agreement, including an open letter calling on TikTok and YouTube to adopt the same framework. According to Meta, teens regularly move among many apps, so similar protections need to extend across the industry. Meta Chief Legal Officer C.J. Mahoney made the same case in an on-camera statement provided to CyberGuy. He said, " Because teens move fluidly across dozens of apps, we need an industry-wide solution." Mahoney also called on TikTok and YouTube to implement the framework right away. From a parent's point of view, Meta's argument is easy to understand. If Instagram closes after two hours while another social platform stays available, some teens may simply move their scrolling somewhere else. That position also helps explain why TikTok and YouTube play such a prominent role in the settlement's financial structure. Limits get tougher if other platforms join Participation from Snap, TikTok and YouTube could trigger stricter Meta limits under the agreement's broader industry-adoption framework. The agreement requires most of its provisions to remain in place for 10 years. However, Meta's Time Limit and Night Mode commitments initially run for five years. If industry peers join the agreement, those commitments extend to 10 years. The defaults would get tougher too. Meta says the Daily Limit would drop to one hour per app. Night Mode would expand from midnight through 6 a.m. to 10 p.m. through 7 a.m. As a result, participation from Meta's rivals could change both the length and strength of the restrictions. Meta wants app stores involved in age checks Meta says social media platforms should not shoulder the entire age-verification process on their own. The company argues that app stores should provide developers with verified age information. According to Meta, that could help apps apply age-appropriate protections more consistently. Meta also supports legislation that would require app stores to verify a user's age and obtain parental approval before a teen downloads an app. That debate could become increasingly important as more platforms introduce age-based restrictions. Independent auditors will check Meta's compliance The agreement also creates outside oversight. An independent auditor will test Meta's compliance and report to participating states. Those reviews will happen annually for five years. Meta says the agreement will also establish an independent social media research foundation. The company says it will provide consented user data to the foundation for research into teen well-being. That outside review could help show whether the protections work once they reach millions of accounts. Tips to help protect your teen right now A judge approved the settlement on Aug. 27. While the new requirements will roll out over the coming months, families can review their teen's social media settings today. Here are several places to start. 1) Set up Meta's parental supervision tools Meta's supervision tools give parents access to additional controls and account information. Once supervision is connected, parents can review available safety settings and manage certain protections. CyberGuy has steps showing you how to activate Instagram's parental supervision tools and link your teen's account. Before changing everything, talk with your teen about the settings you plan to use. Explain what you want to protect and why. 2) Check actual screen time Open the phone's screen-time dashboard and look at the numbers together. You may discover that Instagram or Facebook takes up less time than expected. Another app could be responsible for a much larger share of the day. Then, use those numbers to set limits that reflect how the phone is actually being used. CyberGuy has a deeper guide to phone safety tools for parents, including screen-time controls. 3) Review privacy and contact settings Look at who can follow, message or tag your teen. Meta says it will continue using private defaults for teen Instagram accounts. Facebook will also keep restrictive default settings for teens. Meanwhile, the company plans to make it harder for potentially suspicious adults to find or interact with younger users. Also review followers your teen no longer recognizes. 4) Check content safety settings Meta says teens will remain in age-appropriate content settings by default. The company also plans to continue restricting interactions with accounts it considers inappropriate for younger users. Parents using supervision should check those controls periodically. 5) Use phone-level controls too Facebook and Instagram make up only part of a teen's digital day. Apple Screen Time and Google Family Link can add device-level limits. Those controls become especially useful when a teen moves from one social app to another. As a result, parents can create boundaries that extend beyond Meta's platforms. 6) Create a nighttime phone routine Meta's Night Mode will add an overnight barrier inside Facebook and Instagram. Families can add another layer by charging phones outside bedrooms or keeping them in a shared space overnight. A simple routine can also reduce the nightly debate over when the phone goes away. What these restrictions could mean for teens and parents The two-hour cap will probably grab the most attention because it creates a clear stopping point. However, the bigger change may be how many of these protections will start turned on by default. For teens, that could mean more interruptions during long scrolling sessions, fewer overnight opportunities to browse feeds and less pressure from notifications during school hours. Parents will also gain more visibility when a teen tries to change certain settings. Meanwhile, Meta will face independent compliance reviews during part of the agreement period. Age detection remains a key challenge. If a 15-year-old can easily convince the system that an account belongs to an adult, many of these protections become much easier to avoid. For that reason, the rollout will tell us far more than the announcement alone. Kurt's key takeaways I have watched social media companies add parental controls for years. One recurring problem keeps coming up: Parents have to find the controls before those tools can help. This agreement puts more protections on by default. A two-hour limit that requires parental permission to disable feels very different from another screen-time reminder. The overnight block could also give families some backup when late-night scrolling becomes a constant battle. I understand Meta's argument about TikTok and YouTube too. If one app closes the door while other major platforms remain available, a teen may simply move on to the next feed. Still, the real test comes as these protections roll out over the coming months. I want to see how accurately Meta identifies teen accounts and how difficult these limits are to bypass. Parents should view these tools as backup, not autopilot. Settings can create useful boundaries, but conversations at home still have to carry much of the load. articles.title: Seven arrested after death of newborn baby girl in Sheffield
articles.summary: The baby was pronounced dead at a property in the Wincobank area of Sheffield.
articles.body:
Seven people have been arrested on suspicion of murder after the death of a newborn baby girl in Sheffield, police said.

Officers were called at about 06:00 BST on Sunday to a property on Holywell Heights in the Wincobank area following reports of a concern for the safety of the baby.

South Yorkshire Police said, despite the best efforts of officers and paramedics, the baby was pronounced dead at the scene.

Det Ch Insp Emma Knight confirmed the force was "working to determine the ages of some of those arrested".

She said: "We are aware news of this will be deeply concerning and I want to reassure our local communities that we have a dedicated team of detectives and officers hard at work to ensure justice is secured for the baby girl at the heart of this investigation."

Knight added: "Our investigation is in its early stages and we would like to remind people to avoid speculating about this incident."

articles.title: A small ceramic jug in Russia held 2,600 silver coins for nearly 600 years; its owner’s fate remains a mystery
articles.summary: Rest of World News: A remarkable hoard of 2,600 silver coins has been discovered inside a small ceramic jug in Kolomna, offering a rare glimpse into medieval Russian weal.
articles.body: A remarkable hoard of 2,600 silver coins has been discovered inside a small ceramic jug in Kolomna, offering a rare glimpse into medieval Russian wealth. Archaeologists from the Institute of Archaeology of the Russian Academy of Sciences found the hoard during rescue excavations in the historic centre of the city, near the Kremlin. The coins date mainly to the reigns of Grand Princes Vasily I Dmitrievich and Vasily II Vasilyevich the Dark, with the newest pieces dating to the second half of the 1420s. Researchers say the hoard may also have been concealed during an epidemic that swept through cities of Rus' between 1425 and 1427. The discovery is the largest complete collection of coins from the first half of the 15th century available to researchers. Its contents could help researchers understand wealth, trade and how money was used in medieval Kolomna.2,600 silver coins were discovered inside a medieval ceramic jugThe hoard was found in Kolomna's historic centre during rescue excavations by the Moscow Region expedition of the Institute of Archaeology of the Russian Academy of Sciences. Archaeologists discovered a ceramic jug painted with engobe inside a shallow natural pit on the city's posad(town), close to the Kremlin. There were more than 2,600 silver dengi, the main denomination represented in the collection. The find is considered the largest complete coin hoard from the first half of the 15th century available for study. The quantity and remarkable variety of the coins make the hoard especially valuable for understanding how money circulated locally.What makes the Kolomna hoard different from othersMost of the coins were issued under Grand Princes Vasily I Dmitrievich and Vasily II Vasilyevich the Dark. Very few came from appanage princes. Archaeologists say this pattern reflects Kolomna's own monetary circulation. During the 14th and 15th centuries, the city was a grand princely domain and ranked as the second most important city in the principality after Moscow. The hoard contains a notable group of coins made in Kolomna during the final years of Vasily I's reign. Many carry a flying bird, a design unusually rare in hoards from other regions. Some examples are so uncommon that they were absent from the numismatic collections of the country's largest museums. The discovery adds important material to medieval Russian coinage history.What do the 350 newly identified coin varieties reveal about medieval KolomnaInitial examination has identified more than 350 previously unknown varieties of Kolomna coins. The coins were made using dozens of pairs of dies, with small differences in their designs. By studying these variations, researchers can trace how different types of coins were produced over time. The evidence could help researchers trace minting activity in Kolomna over at least 15 years. It could also help identify the final bird-design coins made there during the last years of Vasily I's reign. With so many locally minted coins in one hoard, the discovery offers a rare picture of the money that circulated in medieval Kolomna.Why was the 2,600-coin fortune never recoveredThe size of the hoard suggests that its owner was wealthy and probably belonged to the upper levels of society. Archaeologists say the person could have been a senior official serving the Grand Duke, an administrator with authority, or a successful merchant. The newest coins were issued by Vasily II in the second half of the 1420s, placing the burial around that period. This date offers a possible explanation for why the money was never recovered. Researchers suggest its owner may have died during one of the epidemic waves that swept through cities of Rus' from 1425 to 1427. The evidence does not establish that the owner was a plague victim, but the timing makes an epidemic a plausible possibility.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.
